hardware_and_gates.pad_hardware: RGB pad LEDs; source uses a 16-position WS2812-class chain
hardware_and_gates.keybed: The 37 physical keys have no LEDs. Logical note-key bitmasks are not physical keybed lights.
hardware_and_gates.buttons: 18 button positions, 19 LED channels in the HAL table. Button LEDs are binary on/off in the SMK platform; no dim/glow layer.
hardware_and_gates.models: BOARD_SMK37 selects this shared path. Source identifies Pro, Elite and MKE-P37 as the same keyboard wiring under different package identities. This is a source statement, not a physical compatibility test by this helper.
hardware_and_gates.model_identity_gate: SMK_MODEL changes reported model identity; default is SMK-37 Pro. No separate Elite LED branch appears in these inspected paths.
hardware_and_gates.default_mapping: Logical B_* roles map through panel.btn, which can be retaught by hardware calibration. Physical captions and fixed bank-button IDs remain distinct.
hardware_and_gates.play_color: HAL channel 16 is PLAY green and channel 18 is PLAY red. Current SMK plat_play_red is a no-op, and plat_leds leaves channel 18 zero. REC has its own red LED at physical button 17; do not borrow the FM-1 red-PLAY behavior.

logical_to_physical.projection: SMK stores k and d, but smk_pads iterates only the sixteen WHITE_NOTE entries. BLACK_KEY bits never reach RGB pads or nonexistent keybed LEDs. Track selection, track mute and part mute identity therefore stay on the LCD.
logical_to_physical.held_input: fm1_in.notes combines keybed knotes and pad pnotes. In the normal UI, k |= ui.keys occurs after content/playhead construction. A held white key or mapped pad becomes bright even if its content bit is off or LIGHTS is OFF, except the division-pad owner replaces the masks afterward.
logical_to_physical.brightness_priority: First build view masks; then OR held ui.keys into k; then an eligible division owner may replace k and d; pass d & ~k to plat_keys_dim; in smk_pads bright wins over dim, then off.
logical_to_physical.grid_gate: Home, Song, drum MIX, PATCH/BT modifiers and ordinary drum contexts use direct GRID mapping. A melodic REC keyboard uses the non-grid row swap unless another direct-grid owner applies. Clip mode has its own vertical flip on top of direct GRID.

normal_rgb_policy.hue: All normal pads use the currently selected part's PART_COL color. Drum MIX uses its visible kit's color. Home pattern pads still share the selected part's hue; they do not use one color per contained part.
normal_rgb_policy.brightness: RGB565 is decoded to 8-bit channels. Bright sends each channel >> 1; dim sends >> 3; off sends zero. These are byte-level arithmetic values, not measured luminance.
normal_rgb_policy.meaning_limits: Normal bright/dim/off and blink/inversion provide meanings. REC, WAIT, mute, held-step and pending cue do not each get a separate normal pad color.
normal_rgb_policy.theme: LIGHT selects the second PART_COLOURS row. Other current palette choices use the first row.

normal_pad_states.content: Selected track's stored hit bits on the current 16-step page; only steps below pattern length light from content.
normal_pad_states.accent_modifier: While CHORD is held, pads show shared kit accent bits instead of selected-track hits.
normal_pad_states.playhead: When seq.playing, the playhead step inverts its content light. A stored hit goes dark at its playhead; an empty step goes bright. This is not an additive white or second-color playhead.
normal_pad_states.selection: Selecting another track changes which pattern the same sixteen pads display. There is no separate selected-track physical light.
normal_pad_states.mute: Pad hit display does not check track mute or part mute. A muted selected track's stored hits remain displayed; mute is communicated on the LCD, not by dimming its entire pad pattern.
normal_pad_states.held: Held white input is ORed after inversion and forces the corresponding normal pad bright. There is no unique held-step color or lock-accepted LED.
normal_pad_states.scope_limit: The drum path applies after Home/MIX precedence, even when another overlay is present. It is not gated to V_SEQ alone.

normal_pad_states.content: Any pattern_used in the visible 16-pattern bank is dim.
normal_pad_states.current: The current pattern for PART_909 is bright if in the visible bank, even when empty. This pad anchor is PART_909, not ui.part.
normal_pad_states.queued: An in-bank PART_909 cue is ORed bright on ui.frame bit 8. An occupied queued pattern alternates dim/bright; an empty queued pattern alternates off/bright. If it is already bright for another reason, no separate blink is guaranteed.
normal_pad_states.partial_cue_limit: A cue only for another part has no separate Home pattern-pad marker in this code.
normal_pad_states.mute_limit: Part mute bits are put on logical BLACK_KEY positions, which have no physical SMK LED projection. LCD lanes carry the part mute identity.
normal_pad_states.stop_wait_limit: The Home cue-light condition does not check seq.playing. If a cue exists while stopped or waiting, its source-defined blink is still eligible. Any proposed static STOP/WAIT cue treatment is a change to record explicitly, not an existing-LED claim.

normal_pad_states.content: Selected voice step/accent lights come from the visible drum kit via drum_step_lights(dm), independent of another selected ui.part.
normal_pad_states.selection_and_mute: Selected mixer channel bright/blinking-muted and other channels dim are logical BLACK_KEY masks, not separate physical SMK track LEDs.

normal_pad_states.content: PARTS builds logical black channel-selection/mute masks. MASTER/WAVE/FX build no content-selection key picture.
normal_pad_states.physical_limit: On the SMK those black masks have no physical projection. Normal held white input can still force a pad bright afterward; that does not mean the view accepted a musical edit.

normal_pad_states.content: G_NOTE steps are bright; G_TIE steps dim; rests off. Playhead inverts the note on/off state. A held white input still wins later.
Logical C positions are dim reference marks; held logical white input becomes bright. They are physical pads, not illuminated piano keys.
normal_pad_states.mapping: With REC on, normal non-grid mapping places low notes on the bottom pad row.

normal_pad_states.content: Its sixteen stored step bits are bright; playhead inverts the current step. Slice availability is placed on eight logical black bits, not separate physical slice lights.

normal_pad_states.content: OFF skips stored-content/cue/reference masks. Held normal white input is still added later; button LEDs remain active.
normal_pad_states.smk_difference: ON requests glow and KEYS does not, but plat_glow is a no-op on the SMK. Thus the FM-1 button-glow distinction is not present in this physical path.
normal_pad_states.overrides: Clip RGB and development pad-calibration output bypass this normal content policy. Division-owner output is fully dark when LIGHTS is OFF.

special_pad_owners.physical_meaning: Each physical pad is the current viewport's vertically flipped APC cell. Its velocity indexes APC40_PAD_OWNER. Velocity zero goes dark. Occupied color is host-derived; press does not prove host launch or recording.
special_pad_owners.brightness: Ordinary occupied shades send level / 2. With SMK_CLIP_IDLE_PAD_LIFT enabled, selected idle shades 7, 11 … 59 send full table level. Queued brightness multiplies by 255 or 0.
special_pad_owners.held_limit: The held clip event remembers its original note for release, but pad RGB follows the currently visible viewport and host feedback. Do not invent a separate held-cell RGB overlay.

sources.claim: Host palette and viewport mapping own pad RGB
Palette provenance; retained source calibration evidence only

special_pad_owners.gates: BOARD_SMK37 && X0X_DEV_WOBBLE && X0X_ORIGINAL_SYNTH, plus actual eligible owner. REC off, Miami Free Play in SEQ/PARA; no question, project transfer, clip mode, SMC popup or pad calibration; PATCH/BT modifiers suspend ownership.
special_pad_owners.physical_meaning: Pads 0–7 select rate; pads 8–11 select shape; pads 12–15 are empty/dark. Available first twelve dim, chosen rate and shape bright when LIGHTS is enabled.
special_pad_owners.priority: The owner replaces both k and d after held-input OR, avoiding fake keybed-note feedback. This is a build-gated route, not a universal drum-pad behavior.

special_pad_owners.gates: X0X_DEV_PADCAL only; source explicitly excludes this page in release builds.
special_pad_owners.physical_meaning: Calibration colors use half-level bytes. Orientation mode lights only its selected first position white. This is a separate diagnostic display, not a live music-state color language.

coordinated_examples.pads: Hardware 0, 4, 8, 12 bright in 909 hue. Other pads dark.
coordinated_examples.buttons: SEQ on; PLAY and REC off; other state-dependent buttons follow their separate roles.

coordinated_examples.preconditions: Same pattern; playing; current step is 5
coordinated_examples.lcd: Step 5 is the playhead; source draws its existing hit/playhead treatment.
coordinated_examples.pads: Pad 4 inverts off because step 5 already has a hit. If pad 4 is held, held-input priority makes it bright instead. An empty playhead step would invert bright.
coordinated_examples.buttons: PLAY is on at step index 4 because 4 % 4 == 0. REC is independent.
coordinated_examples.retention: Keep the existing inversion/held-input behavior honest; no separate source held-step or playhead color is available.

coordinated_examples.pads: P01 pad 0 stays bright. P02 pad 1 alternates dim/bright on frame bit 8. Other occupied patterns dim; empty patterns off.
coordinated_examples.buttons: PATCH on. PLAY and REC show transport/armed state independently.

coordinated_examples.pads: Continue showing selected snare step data. Track mute does not change their hue or suppress all hit lights.
coordinated_examples.buttons: No dedicated selected/muted-track button light. The source's black-key blink has no physical SMK projection.

coordinated_examples.lcd: REC state remains in the instrument context.
coordinated_examples.pads: Step or held-input meanings remain; REC does not recolor normal pads.
coordinated_examples.buttons: SEQ REC red on. SEQ PLAY off; its red channel stays unused.

coordinated_examples.preconditions: Standalone clock-wait predicate true; Home cue exists; LIGHTS enabled
coordinated_examples.lcd: WAIT context and pending cue are separate retained source states. Current cue outline remains eligible for frame-based blinking.
coordinated_examples.pads: Home cue layer remains eligible on frame bit 8. Step display, if shown in another view, uses current eng_step; no timer-generated moving playhead is added by leds().
coordinated_examples.buttons: PLAY uses frame bit 32 in preference to its normal step pulse. REC remains independently armed or off.
coordinated_examples.retention: Any R3 static STOP/WAIT pending-cue treatment needs an explicit change disposition. This helper does not decide it or call the baseline a runtime defect.

coordinated_examples.preconditions: Normal drum path; LIGHTS OFF; no division/clip/calibration owner
coordinated_examples.lcd: Instrument controls and content remain available.
coordinated_examples.pads: Unheld stored content is dark, but a currently held mapped white input remains bright from the final ui.keys layer.
coordinated_examples.buttons: Mode, REC, WAIT and save status remain active; OFF is not a universal physical blackout.
coordinated_examples.retention: Describe the current setting accurately; do not silently broaden it in a visual-only revision.

coordinated_examples.preconditions: Clip mode; host supplies occupied and queued APC feedback
coordinated_examples.lcd: Current clip viewport and host state remain authoritative for clip identity.
coordinated_examples.pads: Host palette supplies cell colors. Queued cells blink with accepted clock or its documented fallback. Held launch release still belongs to the press-time note even after viewport movement.
coordinated_examples.buttons: PLAY/REC use clip feedback, including the source's optimistic press toggle until host feedback replaces it.
coordinated_examples.retention: A press or local lamp toggle is not proof of host launch, recording or durable capture.

preservation_constraints: Keep useful current normal pad scopes: selected-track steps, shared accent under CHORD, Home pattern content/current/cue, and direct GRID placement.
Keep independent mode, transport, record-armed, save and bank button roles; do not overload a normal part hue as recording or mute acceptance.
Never draw or describe physical piano-key lights on Pro/Elite. Logical black-key feedback is LCD-only on this platform.
Treat the existing step playhead as inversion, held input as the same bright level, and mute as a separate LCD fact; any richer replacement is a new proposal requiring affected validation.
Retain exact model/build gates and clip/calibration/division owners; do not import FM-1 glow or red-PLAY behavior.
No current hardware color recognition, visibility, blink discrimination, tactile or audio success is established by this source inventory.
